text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Slovenia newspapers:
- The Slovenian parliament adjourned a vote on whether to back acting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's candidacy to lead a new government until Thursday morning.

- Drnovsek's chances of returning to power signifincantly increased on Wednesday after Ciril Pucko, a Christian Democrat deputy, left his party and said he would vote for centre-left Liberal Democrat Drnovsek, thus securing him a necessary 46th vote.
- Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko resumed operations on Wednesday after being closed down for a week due to a damaged steam pipe.
- Trade with countries that have free-trade agreements with Slovenia makes up 75 percent of the country's foreign trade, the Ministry of Economic Relations and Development said.
- The state-owned bank Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor said its balance sheet assets rose 19 percent in 1996.
- Police had to provide special security for the family of deputy Ciril Pucko because of numerous threats following his announcement he would support Drnovsek.
- The Slovenian Accounting Court which controls public finances said it found irregularities in the accounts of the cities of Ljubljana, Maribor and Novo Mesto.
- Employers and unions on Wednesday started negotiations on a general collective agreement determining work benefits, as previous deal introduced in 1990 expires at the end of May.
- Police said 389 people died in traffic accidents in 1996. It said the number of deaths was below 400 for the first time since 1966.
